recipe: Call `cache` outside of any components to create a version of the function with caching.
trigger_condition: When you need to memoize a function's results in a React Server Component.
evidence: Call `cache` outside of any components to create a version of the function with caching.

recipe: Use `cache` to skip duplicate work when the same expensive computation or data fetch is triggered by multiple components.
trigger_condition: When the same expensive computation or data fetch is triggered by multiple components.

recipe: Preload async data by calling the cached function without `await` before rendering, then `await` it later when the component actually needs the result.
trigger_condition: When you have a long-running asynchronous data fetch that blocks component rendering.
evidence: By caching a long-running data fetch, you can kick off asynchronous work prior to rendering the component.

recipe: When multiple components make the same data fetch through a cached function, only one request is made and the data is shared across all components for the server render.
trigger_condition: When multiple components need the same fetched data during a single server render.
evidence: When multiple components make the same data fetch, only one request is made and the data returned is cached and shared across components.

recipe: Call your memoized function inside a component so it can read from and update the cache; calling it outside a component will evaluate the function but skip the cache entirely.
trigger_condition: You are calling a function wrapped in `cache()` at module level or outside any component render.
evidence: React only provides cache access to the memoized function in a component. When calling <CodeStep step={1}>`getUser`</CodeStep> outside of a component, it will still evaluate the function but not read or update the cache.

recipe: Use `useMemo` to cache an expensive computation in a Client Component across renders, such as memoizing a data transformation within a single component.
trigger_condition: You need to avoid re-running an expensive computation across re-renders of a single Client Component.
evidence: In general, you should use [`useMemo`](/reference/react/useMemo) for caching an expensive computation in a Client Component across renders.

recipe: Use `cache` in Server Components to memoize work that can be shared across multiple component instances, including data fetches.
trigger_condition: You need to memoize work in Server Components that multiple component instances would otherwise repeat.
evidence: In general, you should use `cache` in Server Components to memoize work that can be shared across components.

recipe: Wrap a component in `memo` to prevent re-rendering when its props are unchanged, rather than relying on `useMemo` for component-level memoization.
trigger_condition: A component re-renders unnecessarily because its parent re-renders even though the component's props have not changed.
evidence: You should use [`memo`](reference/react/memo) to prevent a component re-rendering if its props are unchanged.

recipe: When passing non-primitive arguments (objects, arrays, functions) to a memoized function, ensure you pass the same object reference so React's `Object.is` check can find a cache hit.
trigger_condition: Your memoized function is not hitting the cache despite being called with what appears to be the same arguments.
evidence: If your arguments are not [primitives](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Primitive) (ex. objects, functions, arrays), ensure you're passing the same object reference.
